purpose: §305A requires every SE-12 divergence to be classified A (Beta v1 individual product), B (deferred Company/Team), C (shared infrastructure) or D (retired/unknown), so deferred team schema does not drive unnecessary Beta work. This is the INPUT to §305, not its conclusion: entries marked CANDIDATE are reasoned from live-entity presence and from what the §305A workflow suite did and did not touch, and §305 must confirm each against the code that owns it before changing anything.
method: Live entity detection over src/ (explicit @Entity('name') and bare @Entity() with the derived table name). Beta v1 exercise evidence from scripts/test-305a-individual-beta-scope.ts, which drove the complete individual workflow to an issued report on a database built ONLY from migration history — that is, a database missing every production-only table listed here. Exactly one of them broke it.
headline: 18 of the 21 production-only tables HAVE A LIVE ENTITY, so application code can reach tables no migration creates. The Beta v1 workflow nonetheless completed without 20 of the 21; `notifications` is the one that broke, and it broke account deletion.
